title: Will this bag pass the limit?
hook: Half its space is still free.

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a weight limit counts the bag plus everything in it, so empty space does not make a heavy bag any lighter

misconception: If a bag still has free space, it must be under the weight limit.
objective: Capacity in litres and a weight limit answer different questions. The example sums the contents’ masses; unused space does not subtract from that total.

recall.question: Two 30 L bags face an 8 kg limit. One is full of pillows; one is half full of books. Which do you need to weigh?
recall.why: How full a bag is says nothing about its mass, so fullness rules neither bag in nor out. Only the masses decide. The limit is an example, not a carrier's rule.
